# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1618
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1618
- **Title**: gh-1616 [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/ id / folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1616` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 23
- **Additions**: +2488
- **Deletions**: -23
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:10:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T23:35:10Z

## PR Description

Closes #1616
### What changed
Chrome-parity "Load unpacked": a locally picked `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest + assets) is validated, copied into the env's `apps/` store via `AppsStore.installSource`, and appears on the launcher grid with an "unpacked" provenance badge — on web via `showDirectoryPicker`, hidden on hosts without a folder picker.

### Key decisions
- New `UnpackedWidgetLoader` + `UnpackedLoadFlow` (`lib/apps/`) reuse `WidgetPayloadValidator` from publish — one rule set for catalog, publish and local loads
- `installSource` field on `JsAppInfo` (persisted) distinguishes `catalog` / `unpacked` instead of a separate registry
- Conditional-import `FolderPicker` abstraction: web reads `FileSystemDirectoryHandle` entries recursively; stub returns null → entry hidden, not broken
- Overwrite confirmed with a question modal; rejections carry actionable l10n copy (missing manifest, id mismatch, orphan files, unsupported platform) — en/ru added
- Corner badge composes with the existing seed-error badge; entry points: launcher tab row (icon chip) and AppsPanel text button

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/widget_payload_validator_test.dart \
  test/apps/unpacked_loader_test.dart test/apps/unpacked_load_flow_test.dart \
  test/golden/unpacked_load_golden_test.dart
```
Manual (web build): load a folder without `manifest.json` → snack names the missing path; valid folder → confirm → tile on grid with folder badge.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  BTN[Load unpacked buttons] --> FLOW[UnpackedLoadFlow]
  FLOW --> PICK[FolderPicker web/stub]
  FLOW --> VAL[WidgetPayloadValidator]
  VAL -->|valid| CP[UnpackedWidgetLoader copy]
  CP --> STORE[AppsStore.installSource=unpacked]
  STORE --> GRID[Launcher grid + folder badge]
  VAL -->|invalid| SNACK[l10n error snack]
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1618._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_loader.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a whitespace-padded manifest id is validated trimmed but installed untrimmed**

`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` returns the **raw** `manifest['id']` (untrimmed), while `_checkSchema` validates the **trimmed** form (`rawId.trim()` → `_checkId`) and `WidgetManifest.fromJson` also trims. So a manifest like:

```json
{"id": " fa-agents ", "name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}
```

passes validation (the id rule `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is enforced on the trimmed value), and then this line installs it into a **space-padded folder**:

```dart
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: id, // " fa-agents " — written as apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json
  ...
```

Verified locally: `inspection.id` = `" fa-agents "` and the env ends up with `apps/ fa-agents /` + a `.installed.json` key `" fa-agents "` — the stored id violates the very rule the validator just enforced. No traversal risk (regex rejects `/` and `..`), but the widget's stored id no longer matches the id rule, and the folder name carries whitespace everywhere (grid key, `open_app`, records).

Fix (one line, in `UnpackedWidgetLoader.install`):

```dart
final trimmed = id.trim();
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: trimmed,
  version: inspection.version ?? '0.0.0',
  files: inspection.files,
  origin: origin,
);
```

—or reject ids where `id != id.trim()` in the validator with a named `id_invalid` error. A regression test with a padded id belongs in `unpacked_loader_test.dart`.

---

### Thread 2 — `flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_load_flow.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the replace warning is skipped for agent-created apps — their code is overwritten silently**

The replace check keys off the install record:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
...
existingSource: existingApp?.installSource, // null for agent-created apps
```

and the dialog decides `final replaces = existingSource != null;`.

An **agent-created** app (built with Fa via file tools) has **no** `.installed.json` record, so `installSource` is `null` → `replaces` is `false` → the dialog renders as a plain fresh-load confirm ("Load" button, no warning banner), even though confirming **overwrites that app's code** (`installWidget` only protects files whose hashes are recorded — an agent-created app has none, so every file is replaced; only `storage.json` survives).

Ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load confirm still appears, but the explicit replace warning (naming what is being replaced) fires only when the old install came from the catalog or a previous unpacked load. The exact scenario gh-1616 enables — iterate on a widget with Fa, then load a worktree folder with the same id — silently replaces the agent-built code with only a generic confirm.

Fix: treat "an app with this id already exists" as the replace condition, and label the unknown source honestly, e.g.:

```dart
final replaces = existingApp != null;
...
existingSource: existingApp == null
    ? null
    : (existingApp.installSource ?? /* agent-created label */),
```

(the `unpackedLoadReplaceNote` copy needs a third source variant, e.g. "created by the agent"). A test where the existing app has no install record would pin it.

---

### Thread 3 — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/app_launcher_screen.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unpacked badge and the seed-error badge occupy the same corner — one hides the other**

Both badges are `Positioned(top: -3, right: -3)` and stack on the same tile corner:

```dart
child: _maybeUnpackedBadge(
  colors,
  key,
  _maybeSeedErrorBadge(colors, key, _tileIcon(colors, key)),
),
```

`_maybeUnpackedBadge` wraps the seed-error Stack and paints its 14×14 indigo folder badge **after** (on top of) the 16×16 error badge. When both apply — an unpacked-loaded widget whose manifest the agent later edits into garbage (`_appsById[id]?.error != null`) — the doc comment's promise "both can show at once" holds only in the widget tree: visually the folder badge covers the error badge, so the "manifest is broken, tap for the copyable error" affordance disappears exactly when the unpacked widget breaks.

Fix: move the unpacked badge to the opposite corner (e.g. `top: -3, left: -3`), or compose the two indicators side by side in one Stack. Note the error badge is reachable for unpacked apps (it is not demo-only: the `error` branch fires for any unparseable manifest), so this is a real failure-path UI bug, though not data loss.

---

### Thread 4 — `flutter_app/test/golden/unpacked_load_golden_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: unused import — `package:flutter/material.dart`**

```text
warning - unpacked_load_golden_test.dart:13:8 - Unused import:
'package:flutter/material.dart'. ... unused_import
```

The new golden test uses only `flutter_test`, the flow widgets and `Uint8List`. This is the only analyzer finding in the whole PR (everything else in `flutter analyze` for the touched files is pre-existing) — drop line 13 to keep the new file warning-clean.

---

### Thread 5 — `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/apps_panel.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: hardcode `'Load unpacked'` duplicates the new `launcherLoadUnpacked` l10n key**

This PR adds the arb key `launcherLoadUnpacked` ("Load unpacked" / ru "Загрузить папку") and uses it in the launcher tab row — but this second entry point hardcodes the English string:

# gh-1616: [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/<id>/ folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)

## Description

## Goal — unpacked widgets (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **any local `apps/<id>/` folder (`manifest.json` + `widget.js`) can be loaded into the fa Chrome extension like Chrome's "Load unpacked" — it appears in the Apps tab, renders via `jsr.render`, updates on schedule, and survives restarts — no catalog publication needed.**

Today widgets come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Apps → Get widgets → Install). There is no way to load a local widget (e.g. a worktree copy of a widget under development), which blocks the whole widget-dev loop.

## Why this framing
- Chrome parity is the UX contract: unpacked = local folder, loaded once, persisted while the folder exists, invalidated loudly when it breaks. Retracted framing: "dev server / hot reload" — excluded (see non-goals); this card is load + validate + persist.

## Architecture
- Components: Apps tab (list + install sources), the unpacked-loader (file picker / folder entry), the **shared widget validator** (id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, manifest schema, entry presence — the same validator #1614 introduces for storage reads), the web `ExecutionEnv` storage (OPFS) as the persistence layer, `jsr.render` boot path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (same shape):** an unpacked widget is stored exactly like a catalog-installed one (`apps/<id>/`), so boot, updates (`refreshSeconds`), and the Apps tab need zero special cases.
  - **I2 (declared capability only):** a widget runs with only what its `manifest.json` declares; loading a folder grants no filesystem or host access beyond the copied files.
  - **I3 (provenance):** apps carry an install source (`catalog` | `unpacked`), surfaced in the UI; uninstall/reinstall semantics per source (unpacked reinstall = re-pick folder).

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Load unpacked" folder picker → validate → store → appear in Apps | **core** | chrome-like; errors name field + path (shared validator) |
| Persistence across extension restarts | **core** | OPFS copy, not a live folder mount — Chrome-unpacked-like while-folder semantics approximated: survives restarts; folder edits require explicit re-load |
| Updates from folder | second tier | explicit "reload from folder" button (no watchers in MV3 service worker) |
| Path-in-settings alternative to the picker | second tier | for headless repro |
| Uninstall / replace-existing-id flow | **core** | overwriting an existing id requires explicit confirm |
| Hot reload / folder watching | excluded | MV3 lifecycle makes watchers unreliable; explicit reload is honest |
| Widget signature/allowlist | excluded | trust model = user loads their own folder; noted in security |

## Security (untrusted widget code — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: the loaded `manifest.json` and `widget.js` are **hostile until validated**.
- Impossible-by-construction: a widget has no fa-API surface beyond `jsr.render`; no fs access exists on the extension host to grant; network is the page-level fetch the manifest declares — the loader cannot mint extra permissions (I2). Id validation + root clamping (from #1614) prevent `apps/…` escapes.
- Instruction hierarchy: widget text is DATA for the agent, never instructions (existing chat-widget rules); a widget cannot steer the agent that renders it.
- Exfiltration gate: a widget's declared network origins are shown at load time ("this widget will fetch from 127.0.0.1:8765") — the load confirmation is the user grant.
- Defense in depth: validation is hygiene; the real boundary is that no widget-escapable API exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — "Load unpacked" on the Apps tab: pick a folder → validated → visible in Apps with `unpacked` provenance → renders via `jsr.render`, updates on `refreshSeconds`.
- **AC2** — invalid payloads produce named errors (bad id, missing entry file, malformed manifest) — never `app entry not found` raw (#1614's validator, shared).
- **AC3** — restart the extension: the unpacked widget persists and boots.
- **AC4** — catalog install (IstiN/fa_widgets) works unchanged; both sources coexist in the list; replacing an existing id asks for confirmation.
- **AC5** — the loader test-case fixture: `fa-agents` widget (from the local worktree) loads, appears, and renders data from a local feed at `127.0.0.1:8765`.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — validator: id regex, manifest schema, entry presence; traversal ids rejected.
- `IT-*` — web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`: load → store → boot → refresh cycle; replace-id confirm; restart persistence (re-open env).
- `E2E-*` — extension e2e: load unpacked via the real UI (file-picker stubbed), widget appears and renders; catalog install REG-unchanged (AC4); restart persistence (AC3).
- `REG-1` — CI: UT+IT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart` / Apps tab; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — folder picked, then folder deleted before load completes → honest error. **E2** — manifest declares a fetch origin the user wasn't shown → shown-or-blocked (E2E asserts the confirmation lists it). **E3** — two sources, same id — replace flow (AC4). **E4** — huge widget.js → size cap with clear message.

## Non-goals
- No hot reload/watchers; no widget marketplace changes; no new widget API surface; no signing infrastructure; no cross-device sync.

## Open questions
1. Load-time network-origin confirmation: blocking dialog (Chrome-style) vs settings toggle? *Sketched default: blocking on first load, remembered per widget.*
2. Should unpacked widgets also be loadable from the CLI (`fa widgets load <dir>`) for CI? *Default: second tier.*

## References
- #1616 (original: YuryBY, with the fa-agents acceptance case), #1614 (shared validator + storage namespace), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, browser_ext Apps tab, IstiN/fa_widgets catalog.

Requirements: UI entry point, same jsr.render/refresh behavior, id+manifest validation with clear errors (#1614), manifest-scoped permissions only, persistence across restarts, no catalog regression. Acceptance fixture: `fa-agents` widget rendering a local feed on 127.0.0.1:8765.
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1618
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1618
- **Title**: gh-1616 [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/ id / folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1616` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 23
- **Additions**: +2488
- **Deletions**: -23
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:10:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T23:35:10Z

## PR Description

Closes #1616
### What changed
Chrome-parity "Load unpacked": a locally picked `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest + assets) is validated, copied into the env's `apps/` store via `AppsStore.installSource`, and appears on the launcher grid with an "unpacked" provenance badge — on web via `showDirectoryPicker`, hidden on hosts without a folder picker.

### Key decisions
- New `UnpackedWidgetLoader` + `UnpackedLoadFlow` (`lib/apps/`) reuse `WidgetPayloadValidator` from publish — one rule set for catalog, publish and local loads
- `installSource` field on `JsAppInfo` (persisted) distinguishes `catalog` / `unpacked` instead of a separate registry
- Conditional-import `FolderPicker` abstraction: web reads `FileSystemDirectoryHandle` entries recursively; stub returns null → entry hidden, not broken
- Overwrite confirmed with a question modal; rejections carry actionable l10n copy (missing manifest, id mismatch, orphan files, unsupported platform) — en/ru added
- Corner badge composes with the existing seed-error badge; entry points: launcher tab row (icon chip) and AppsPanel text button

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/widget_payload_validator_test.dart \
  test/apps/unpacked_loader_test.dart test/apps/unpacked_load_flow_test.dart \
  test/golden/unpacked_load_golden_test.dart
```
Manual (web build): load a folder without `manifest.json` → snack names the missing path; valid folder → confirm → tile on grid with folder badge.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  BTN[Load unpacked buttons] --> FLOW[UnpackedLoadFlow]
  FLOW --> PICK[FolderPicker web/stub]
  FLOW --> VAL[WidgetPayloadValidator]
  VAL -->|valid| CP[UnpackedWidgetLoader copy]
  CP --> STORE[AppsStore.installSource=unpacked]
  STORE --> GRID[Launcher grid + folder badge]
  VAL -->|invalid| SNACK[l10n error snack]
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1618._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_loader.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a whitespace-padded manifest id is validated trimmed but installed untrimmed**

`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` returns the **raw** `manifest['id']` (untrimmed), while `_checkSchema` validates the **trimmed** form (`rawId.trim()` → `_checkId`) and `WidgetManifest.fromJson` also trims. So a manifest like:

```json
{"id": " fa-agents ", "name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}
```

passes validation (the id rule `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is enforced on the trimmed value), and then this line installs it into a **space-padded folder**:

```dart
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: id, // " fa-agents " — written as apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json
  ...
```

Verified locally: `inspection.id` = `" fa-agents "` and the env ends up with `apps/ fa-agents /` + a `.installed.json` key `" fa-agents "` — the stored id violates the very rule the validator just enforced. No traversal risk (regex rejects `/` and `..`), but the widget's stored id no longer matches the id rule, and the folder name carries whitespace everywhere (grid key, `open_app`, records).

Fix (one line, in `UnpackedWidgetLoader.install`):

```dart
final trimmed = id.trim();
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: trimmed,
  version: inspection.version ?? '0.0.0',
  files: inspection.files,
  origin: origin,
);
```

—or reject ids where `id != id.trim()` in the validator with a named `id_invalid` error. A regression test with a padded id belongs in `unpacked_loader_test.dart`.

---

### Thread 2 — `flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_load_flow.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the replace warning is skipped for agent-created apps — their code is overwritten silently**

The replace check keys off the install record:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
...
existingSource: existingApp?.installSource, // null for agent-created apps
```

and the dialog decides `final replaces = existingSource != null;`.

An **agent-created** app (built with Fa via file tools) has **no** `.installed.json` record, so `installSource` is `null` → `replaces` is `false` → the dialog renders as a plain fresh-load confirm ("Load" button, no warning banner), even though confirming **overwrites that app's code** (`installWidget` only protects files whose hashes are recorded — an agent-created app has none, so every file is replaced; only `storage.json` survives).

Ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load confirm still appears, but the explicit replace warning (naming what is being replaced) fires only when the old install came from the catalog or a previous unpacked load. The exact scenario gh-1616 enables — iterate on a widget with Fa, then load a worktree folder with the same id — silently replaces the agent-built code with only a generic confirm.

Fix: treat "an app with this id already exists" as the replace condition, and label the unknown source honestly, e.g.:

```dart
final replaces = existingApp != null;
...
existingSource: existingApp == null
    ? null
    : (existingApp.installSource ?? /* agent-created label */),
```

(the `unpackedLoadReplaceNote` copy needs a third source variant, e.g. "created by the agent"). A test where the existing app has no install record would pin it.

---

### Thread 3 — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/app_launcher_screen.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unpacked badge and the seed-error badge occupy the same corner — one hides the other**

Both badges are `Positioned(top: -3, right: -3)` and stack on the same tile corner:

```dart
child: _maybeUnpackedBadge(
  colors,
  key,
  _maybeSeedErrorBadge(colors, key, _tileIcon(colors, key)),
),
```

`_maybeUnpackedBadge` wraps the seed-error Stack and paints its 14×14 indigo folder badge **after** (on top of) the 16×16 error badge. When both apply — an unpacked-loaded widget whose manifest the agent later edits into garbage (`_appsById[id]?.error != null`) — the doc comment's promise "both can show at once" holds only in the widget tree: visually the folder badge covers the error badge, so the "manifest is broken, tap for the copyable error" affordance disappears exactly when the unpacked widget breaks.

Fix: move the unpacked badge to the opposite corner (e.g. `top: -3, left: -3`), or compose the two indicators side by side in one Stack. Note the error badge is reachable for unpacked apps (it is not demo-only: the `error` branch fires for any unparseable manifest), so this is a real failure-path UI bug, though not data loss.

---

### Thread 4 — `flutter_app/test/golden/unpacked_load_golden_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: unused import — `package:flutter/material.dart`**

```text
warning - unpacked_load_golden_test.dart:13:8 - Unused import:
'package:flutter/material.dart'. ... unused_import
```

The new golden test uses only `flutter_test`, the flow widgets and `Uint8List`. This is the only analyzer finding in the whole PR (everything else in `flutter analyze` for the touched files is pre-existing) — drop line 13 to keep the new file warning-clean.

💡 **SUGGESTION: hardcode `'Load unpacked'` duplicates the new `launcherLoadUnpacked` l10n key**

This PR adds the arb key `launcherLoadUnpacked` ("Load unpacked" / ru "Загрузить папку") and uses it in the launcher tab row — but this second entry point hardcodes the English string:

```dart

# gh-1616: [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/<id>/ folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)

## Description

## Goal — unpacked widgets (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **any local `apps/<id>/` folder (`manifest.json` + `widget.js`) can be loaded into the fa Chrome extension like Chrome's "Load unpacked" — it appears in the Apps tab, renders via `jsr.render`, updates on schedule, and survives restarts — no catalog publication needed.**

Today widgets come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Apps → Get widgets → Install). There is no way to load a local widget (e.g. a worktree copy of a widget under development), which blocks the whole widget-dev loop.

## Why this framing
- Chrome parity is the UX contract: unpacked = local folder, loaded once, persisted while the folder exists, invalidated loudly when it breaks. Retracted framing: "dev server / hot reload" — excluded (see non-goals); this card is load + validate + persist.

## Architecture
- Components: Apps tab (list + install sources), the unpacked-loader (file picker / folder entry), the **shared widget validator** (id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, manifest schema, entry presence — the same validator #1614 introduces for storage reads), the web `ExecutionEnv` storage (OPFS) as the persistence layer, `jsr.render` boot path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (same shape):** an unpacked widget is stored exactly like a catalog-installed one (`apps/<id>/`), so boot, updates (`refreshSeconds`), and the Apps tab need zero special cases.
  - **I2 (declared capability only):** a widget runs with only what its `manifest.json` declares; loading a folder grants no filesystem or host access beyond the copied files.
  - **I3 (provenance):** apps carry an install source (`catalog` | `unpacked`), surfaced in the UI; uninstall/reinstall semantics per source (unpacked reinstall = re-pick folder).

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Load unpacked" folder picker → validate → store → appear in Apps | **core** | chrome-like; errors name field + path (shared validator) |
| Persistence across extension restarts | **core** | OPFS copy, not a live folder mount — Chrome-unpacked-like while-folder semantics approximated: survives restarts; folder edits require explicit re-load |
| Updates from folder | second tier | explicit "reload from folder" button (no watchers in MV3 service worker) |
| Path-in-settings alternative to the picker | second tier | for headless repro |
| Uninstall / replace-existing-id flow | **core** | overwriting an existing id requires explicit confirm |
| Hot reload / folder watching | excluded | MV3 lifecycle makes watchers unreliable; explicit reload is honest |
| Widget signature/allowlist | excluded | trust model = user loads their own folder; noted in security |

## Security (untrusted widget code — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: the loaded `manifest.json` and `widget.js` are **hostile until validated**.
- Impossible-by-construction: a widget has no fa-API surface beyond `jsr.render`; no fs access exists on the extension host to grant; network is the page-level fetch the manifest declares — the loader cannot mint extra permissions (I2). Id validation + root clamping (from #1614) prevent `apps/…` escapes.
- Instruction hierarchy: widget text is DATA for the agent, never instructions (existing chat-widget rules); a widget cannot steer the agent that renders it.
- Exfiltration gate: a widget's declared network origins are shown at load time ("this widget will fetch from 127.0.0.1:8765") — the load confirmation is the user grant.
- Defense in depth: validation is hygiene; the real boundary is that no widget-escapable API exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — "Load unpacked" on the Apps tab: pick a folder → validated → visible in Apps with `unpacked` provenance → renders via `jsr.render`, updates on `refreshSeconds`.
- **AC2** — invalid payloads produce named errors (bad id, missing entry file, malformed manifest) — never `app entry not found` raw (#1614's validator, shared).
- **AC3** — restart the extension: the unpacked widget persists and boots.
- **AC4** — catalog install (IstiN/fa_widgets) works unchanged; both sources coexist in the list; replacing an existing id asks for confirmation.
- **AC5** — the loader test-case fixture: `fa-agents` widget (from the local worktree) loads, appears, and renders data from a local feed at `127.0.0.1:8765`.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — validator: id regex, manifest schema, entry presence; traversal ids rejected.
- `IT-*` — web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`: load → store → boot → refresh cycle; replace-id confirm; restart persistence (re-open env).
- `E2E-*` — extension e2e: load unpacked via the real UI (file-picker stubbed), widget appears and renders; catalog install REG-unchanged (AC4); restart persistence (AC3).
- `REG-1` — CI: UT+IT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart` / Apps tab; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — folder picked, then folder deleted before load completes → honest error. **E2** — manifest declares a fetch origin the user wasn't shown → shown-or-blocked (E2E asserts the confirmation lists it). **E3** — two sources, same id — replace flow (AC4). **E4** — huge widget.js → size cap with clear message.

## Non-goals
- No hot reload/watchers; no widget marketplace changes; no new widget API surface; no signing infrastructure; no cross-device sync.

## Open questions
1. Load-time network-origin confirmation: blocking dialog (Chrome-style) vs settings toggle? *Sketched default: blocking on first load, remembered per widget.*
2. Should unpacked widgets also be loadable from the CLI (`fa widgets load <dir>`) for CI? *Default: second tier.*

## References
- #1616 (original: YuryBY, with the fa-agents acceptance case), #1614 (shared validator + storage namespace), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, browser_ext Apps tab, IstiN/fa_widgets catalog.

---

<details><summary>Original report (YuryBY, condensed)</summary>
Widgets in the extension come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Install → Get widgets). Need: load a local `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest.json + widget.js) into the extension, chrome-unpacked style. Requirements: UI entry point, same jsr.render/refresh behavior, id+manifest validation with clear errors (#1614), manifest-scoped permissions only, persistence across restarts, no catalog regression. Acceptance fixture: `fa-agents` widget rendering a local feed on 127.0.0.1:8765.
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1618
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1618
- **Title**: gh-1616 [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/ id / folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1616` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 23
- **Additions**: +2488
- **Deletions**: -23
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:10:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T23:35:10Z

## PR Description

Closes #1616
### What changed
Chrome-parity "Load unpacked": a locally picked `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest + assets) is validated, copied into the env's `apps/` store via `AppsStore.installSource`, and appears on the launcher grid with an "unpacked" provenance badge — on web via `showDirectoryPicker`, hidden on hosts without a folder picker.

### Key decisions
- New `UnpackedWidgetLoader` + `UnpackedLoadFlow` (`lib/apps/`) reuse `WidgetPayloadValidator` from publish — one rule set for catalog, publish and local loads
- `installSource` field on `JsAppInfo` (persisted) distinguishes `catalog` / `unpacked` instead of a separate registry
- Conditional-import `FolderPicker` abstraction: web reads `FileSystemDirectoryHandle` entries recursively; stub returns null → entry hidden, not broken
- Overwrite confirmed with a question modal; rejections carry actionable l10n copy (missing manifest, id mismatch, orphan files, unsupported platform) — en/ru added
- Corner badge composes with the existing seed-error badge; entry points: launcher tab row (icon chip) and AppsPanel text button

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/widget_payload_validator_test.dart \
  test/apps/unpacked_loader_test.dart test/apps/unpacked_load_flow_test.dart \
  test/golden/unpacked_load_golden_test.dart
```
Manual (web build): load a folder without `manifest.json` → snack names the missing path; valid folder → confirm → tile on grid with folder badge.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  BTN[Load unpacked buttons] --> FLOW[UnpackedLoadFlow]
  FLOW --> PICK[FolderPicker web/stub]
  FLOW --> VAL[WidgetPayloadValidator]
  VAL -->|valid| CP[UnpackedWidgetLoader copy]
  CP --> STORE[AppsStore.installSource=unpacked]
  STORE --> GRID[Launcher grid + folder badge]
  VAL -->|invalid| SNACK[l10n error snack]
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1618._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_loader.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a whitespace-padded manifest id is validated trimmed but installed untrimmed**

`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` returns the **raw** `manifest['id']` (untrimmed), while `_checkSchema` validates the **trimmed** form (`rawId.trim()` → `_checkId`) and `WidgetManifest.fromJson` also trims. So a manifest like:

```json
{"id": " fa-agents ", "name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}
```

passes validation (the id rule `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is enforced on the trimmed value), and then this line installs it into a **space-padded folder**:

```dart
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: id, // " fa-agents " — written as apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json
  ...
```

Verified locally: `inspection.id` = `" fa-agents "` and the env ends up with `apps/ fa-agents /` + a `.installed.json` key `" fa-agents "` — the stored id violates the very rule the validator just enforced. No traversal risk (regex rejects `/` and `..`), but the widget's stored id no longer matches the id rule, and the folder name carries whitespace everywhere (grid key, `open_app`, records).

Fix (one line, in `UnpackedWidgetLoader.install`):

```dart
final trimmed = id.trim();
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: trimmed,
  version: inspection.version ?? '0.0.0',
  files: inspection.files,
  origin: origin,
);
```

—or reject ids where `id != id.trim()` in the validator with a named `id_invalid` error. A regression test with a padded id belongs in `unpacked_loader_test.dart`.

---

### Thread 2 — `flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_load_flow.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the replace warning is skipped for agent-created apps — their code is overwritten silently**

The replace check keys off the install record:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
...
existingSource: existingApp?.installSource, // null for agent-created apps
```

and the dialog decides `final replaces = existingSource != null;`.

An **agent-created** app (built with Fa via file tools) has **no** `.installed.json` record, so `installSource` is `null` → `replaces` is `false` → the dialog renders as a plain fresh-load confirm ("Load" button, no warning banner), even though confirming **overwrites that app's code** (`installWidget` only protects files whose hashes are recorded — an agent-created app has none, so every file is replaced; only `storage.json` survives).

Ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load confirm still appears, but the explicit replace warning (naming what is being replaced) fires only when the old install came from the catalog or a previous unpacked load. The exact scenario gh-1616 enables — iterate on a widget with Fa, then load a worktree folder with the same id — silently replaces the agent-built code with only a generic confirm.

Fix: treat "an app with this id already exists" as the replace condition, and label the unknown source honestly, e.g.:

```dart
final replaces = existingApp != null;
...
existingSource: existingApp == null
    ? null
    : (existingApp.installSource ?? /* agent-created label */),
```

(the `unpackedLoadReplaceNote` copy needs a third source variant, e.g. "created by the agent"). A test where the existing app has no install record would pin it.

---

### Thread 3 — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/app_launcher_screen.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unpacked badge and the seed-error badge occupy the same corner — one hides the other**

Both badges are `Positioned(top: -3, right: -3)` and stack on the same tile corner:

```dart
child: _maybeUnpackedBadge(
  colors,
  key,
  _maybeSeedErrorBadge(colors, key, _tileIcon(colors, key)),
),
```

`_maybeUnpackedBadge` wraps the seed-error Stack and paints its 14×14 indigo folder badge **after** (on top of) the 16×16 error badge. When both apply — an unpacked-loaded widget whose manifest the agent later edits into garbage (`_appsById[id]?.error != null`) — the doc comment's promise "both can show at once" holds only in the widget tree: visually the folder badge covers the error badge, so the "manifest is broken, tap for the copyable error" affordance disappears exactly when the unpacked widget breaks.

Fix: move the unpacked badge to the opposite corner (e.g. `top: -3, left: -3`), or compose the two indicators side by side in one Stack. Note the error badge is reachable for unpacked apps (it is not demo-only: the `error` branch fires for any unparseable manifest), so this is a real failure-path UI bug, though not data loss.

---

### Thread 4 — `flutter_app/test/golden/unpacked_load_golden_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: unused import — `package:flutter/material.dart`**

```text
warning - unpacked_load_golden_test.dart:13:8 - Unused import:
'package:flutter/material.dart'. ... unused_import
```

The new golden test uses only `flutter_test`, the flow widgets and `Uint8List`. This is the only analyzer finding in the whole PR (everything else in `flutter analyze` for the touched files is pre-existing) — drop line 13 to keep the new file warning-clean.

💡 **SUGGESTION: hardcode `'Load unpacked'` duplicates the new `launcherLoadUnpacked` l10n key**

This PR adds the arb key `launcherLoadUnpacked` ("Load unpacked" / ru "Загрузить папку") and uses it in the launcher tab row — but this second entry point hardcodes the English string:

```dart

# gh-1616: [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/<id>/ folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)

## Description

## Goal — unpacked widgets (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **any local `apps/<id>/` folder (`manifest.json` + `widget.js`) can be loaded into the fa Chrome extension like Chrome's "Load unpacked" — it appears in the Apps tab, renders via `jsr.render`, updates on schedule, and survives restarts — no catalog publication needed.**

Today widgets come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Apps → Get widgets → Install). There is no way to load a local widget (e.g. a worktree copy of a widget under development), which blocks the whole widget-dev loop.

## Why this framing
- Chrome parity is the UX contract: unpacked = local folder, loaded once, persisted while the folder exists, invalidated loudly when it breaks. Retracted framing: "dev server / hot reload" — excluded (see non-goals); this card is load + validate + persist.

## Architecture
- Components: Apps tab (list + install sources), the unpacked-loader (file picker / folder entry), the **shared widget validator** (id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, manifest schema, entry presence — the same validator #1614 introduces for storage reads), the web `ExecutionEnv` storage (OPFS) as the persistence layer, `jsr.render` boot path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (same shape):** an unpacked widget is stored exactly like a catalog-installed one (`apps/<id>/`), so boot, updates (`refreshSeconds`), and the Apps tab need zero special cases.
  - **I2 (declared capability only):** a widget runs with only what its `manifest.json` declares; loading a folder grants no filesystem or host access beyond the copied files.
  - **I3 (provenance):** apps carry an install source (`catalog` | `unpacked`), surfaced in the UI; uninstall/reinstall semantics per source (unpacked reinstall = re-pick folder).

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Load unpacked" folder picker → validate → store → appear in Apps | **core** | chrome-like; errors name field + path (shared validator) |
| Persistence across extension restarts | **core** | OPFS copy, not a live folder mount — Chrome-unpacked-like while-folder semantics approximated: survives restarts; folder edits require explicit re-load |
| Updates from folder | second tier | explicit "reload from folder" button (no watchers in MV3 service worker) |
| Path-in-settings alternative to the picker | second tier | for headless repro |
| Uninstall / replace-existing-id flow | **core** | overwriting an existing id requires explicit confirm |
| Hot reload / folder watching | excluded | MV3 lifecycle makes watchers unreliable; explicit reload is honest |
| Widget signature/allowlist | excluded | trust model = user loads their own folder; noted in security |

## Security (untrusted widget code — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: the loaded `manifest.json` and `widget.js` are **hostile until validated**.
- Impossible-by-construction: a widget has no fa-API surface beyond `jsr.render`; no fs access exists on the extension host to grant; network is the page-level fetch the manifest declares — the loader cannot mint extra permissions (I2). Id validation + root clamping (from #1614) prevent `apps/…` escapes.
- Instruction hierarchy: widget text is DATA for the agent, never instructions (existing chat-widget rules); a widget cannot steer the agent that renders it.
- Exfiltration gate: a widget's declared network origins are shown at load time ("this widget will fetch from 127.0.0.1:8765") — the load confirmation is the user grant.
- Defense in depth: validation is hygiene; the real boundary is that no widget-escapable API exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — "Load unpacked" on the Apps tab: pick a folder → validated → visible in Apps with `unpacked` provenance → renders via `jsr.render`, updates on `refreshSeconds`.
- **AC2** — invalid payloads produce named errors (bad id, missing entry file, malformed manifest) — never `app entry not found` raw (#1614's validator, shared).
- **AC3** — restart the extension: the unpacked widget persists and boots.
- **AC4** — catalog install (IstiN/fa_widgets) works unchanged; both sources coexist in the list; replacing an existing id asks for confirmation.
- **AC5** — the loader test-case fixture: `fa-agents` widget (from the local worktree) loads, appears, and renders data from a local feed at `127.0.0.1:8765`.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — validator: id regex, manifest schema, entry presence; traversal ids rejected.
- `IT-*` — web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`: load → store → boot → refresh cycle; replace-id confirm; restart persistence (re-open env).
- `E2E-*` — extension e2e: load unpacked via the real UI (file-picker stubbed), widget appears and renders; catalog install REG-unchanged (AC4); restart persistence (AC3).
- `REG-1` — CI: UT+IT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart` / Apps tab; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — folder picked, then folder deleted before load completes → honest error. **E2** — manifest declares a fetch origin the user wasn't shown → shown-or-blocked (E2E asserts the confirmation lists it). **E3** — two sources, same id — replace flow (AC4). **E4** — huge widget.js → size cap with clear message.

## Non-goals
- No hot reload/watchers; no widget marketplace changes; no new widget API surface; no signing infrastructure; no cross-device sync.

## Open questions
1. Load-time network-origin confirmation: blocking dialog (Chrome-style) vs settings toggle? *Sketched default: blocking on first load, remembered per widget.*
2. Should unpacked widgets also be loadable from the CLI (`fa widgets load <dir>`) for CI? *Default: second tier.*

## References
- #1616 (original: YuryBY, with the fa-agents acceptance case), #1614 (shared validator + storage namespace), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, browser_ext Apps tab, IstiN/fa_widgets catalog.

---

<details><summary>Original report (YuryBY, condensed)</summary>
Widgets in the extension come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Install → Get widgets). Need: load a local `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest.json + widget.js) into the extension, chrome-unpacked style. Requirements: UI entry point, same jsr.render/refresh behavior, id+manifest validation with clear errors (#1614), manifest-scoped permissions only, persistence across restarts, no catalog regression. Acceptance fixture: `fa-agents` widget rendering a local feed on 127.0.0.1:8765.
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1618
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1618
- **Title**: gh-1616 [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/ id / folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1616` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 23
- **Additions**: +2488
- **Deletions**: -23
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:10:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T23:35:10Z

## PR Description

Closes #1616
### What changed
Chrome-parity "Load unpacked": a locally picked `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest + assets) is validated, copied into the env's `apps/` store via `AppsStore.installSource`, and appears on the launcher grid with an "unpacked" provenance badge — on web via `showDirectoryPicker`, hidden on hosts without a folder picker.

### Key decisions
- New `UnpackedWidgetLoader` + `UnpackedLoadFlow` (`lib/apps/`) reuse `WidgetPayloadValidator` from publish — one rule set for catalog, publish and local loads
- `installSource` field on `JsAppInfo` (persisted) distinguishes `catalog` / `unpacked` instead of a separate registry
- Conditional-import `FolderPicker` abstraction: web reads `FileSystemDirectoryHandle` entries recursively; stub returns null → entry hidden, not broken
- Overwrite confirmed with a question modal; rejections carry actionable l10n copy (missing manifest, id mismatch, orphan files, unsupported platform) — en/ru added
- Corner badge composes with the existing seed-error badge; entry points: launcher tab row (icon chip) and AppsPanel text button

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/widget_payload_validator_test.dart \
  test/apps/unpacked_loader_test.dart test/apps/unpacked_load_flow_test.dart \
  test/golden/unpacked_load_golden_test.dart
```
Manual (web build): load a folder without `manifest.json` → snack names the missing path; valid folder → confirm → tile on grid with folder badge.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  BTN[Load unpacked buttons] --> FLOW[UnpackedLoadFlow]
  FLOW --> PICK[FolderPicker web/stub]
  FLOW --> VAL[WidgetPayloadValidator]
  VAL -->|valid| CP[UnpackedWidgetLoader copy]
  CP --> STORE[AppsStore.installSource=unpacked]
  STORE --> GRID[Launcher grid + folder badge]
  VAL -->|invalid| SNACK[l10n error snack]
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1618._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_loader.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a whitespace-padded manifest id is validated trimmed but installed untrimmed**

`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` returns the **raw** `manifest['id']` (untrimmed), while `_checkSchema` validates the **trimmed** form (`rawId.trim()` → `_checkId`) and `WidgetManifest.fromJson` also trims. So a manifest like:

```json
{"id": " fa-agents ", "name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}
```

passes validation (the id rule `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is enforced on the trimmed value), and then this line installs it into a **space-padded folder**:

```dart
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: id, // " fa-agents " — written as apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json
  ...
```

Verified locally: `inspection.id` = `" fa-agents "` and the env ends up with `apps/ fa-agents /` + a `.installed.json` key `" fa-agents "` — the stored id violates the very rule the validator just enforced. No traversal risk (regex rejects `/` and `..`), but the widget's stored id no longer matches the id rule, and the folder name carries whitespace everywhere (grid key, `open_app`, records).

Fix (one line, in `UnpackedWidgetLoader.install`):

```dart
final trimmed = id.trim();
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: trimmed,
  version: inspection.version ?? '0.0.0',
  files: inspection.files,
  origin: origin,
);
```

—or reject ids where `id != id.trim()` in the validator with a named `id_invalid` error. A regression test with a padded id belongs in `unpacked_loader_test.dart`.

---

### Thread 2 — `flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_load_flow.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the replace warning is skipped for agent-created apps — their code is overwritten silently**

The replace check keys off the install record:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
...
existingSource: existingApp?.installSource, // null for agent-created apps
```

and the dialog decides `final replaces = existingSource != null;`.

An **agent-created** app (built with Fa via file tools) has **no** `.installed.json` record, so `installSource` is `null` → `replaces` is `false` → the dialog renders as a plain fresh-load confirm ("Load" button, no warning banner), even though confirming **overwrites that app's code** (`installWidget` only protects files whose hashes are recorded — an agent-created app has none, so every file is replaced; only `storage.json` survives).

Ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load confirm still appears, but the explicit replace warning (naming what is being replaced) fires only when the old install came from the catalog or a previous unpacked load. The exact scenario gh-1616 enables — iterate on a widget with Fa, then load a worktree folder with the same id — silently replaces the agent-built code with only a generic confirm.

Fix: treat "an app with this id already exists" as the replace condition, and label the unknown source honestly, e.g.:

```dart
final replaces = existingApp != null;
...
existingSource: existingApp == null
    ? null
    : (existingApp.installSource ?? /* agent-created label */),
```

(the `unpackedLoadReplaceNote` copy needs a third source variant, e.g. "created by the agent"). A test where the existing app has no install record would pin it.

---

### Thread 3 — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/app_launcher_screen.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unpacked badge and the seed-error badge occupy the same corner — one hides the other**

Both badges are `Positioned(top: -3, right: -3)` and stack on the same tile corner:

```dart
child: _maybeUnpackedBadge(
  colors,
  key,
  _maybeSeedErrorBadge(colors, key, _tileIcon(colors, key)),
),
```

`_maybeUnpackedBadge` wraps the seed-error Stack and paints its 14×14 indigo folder badge **after** (on top of) the 16×16 error badge. When both apply — an unpacked-loaded widget whose manifest the agent later edits into garbage (`_appsById[id]?.error != null`) — the doc comment's promise "both can show at once" holds only in the widget tree: visually the folder badge covers the error badge, so the "manifest is broken, tap for the copyable error" affordance disappears exactly when the unpacked widget breaks.

Fix: move the unpacked badge to the opposite corner (e.g. `top: -3, left: -3`), or compose the two indicators side by side in one Stack. Note the error badge is reachable for unpacked apps (it is not demo-only: the `error` branch fires for any unparseable manifest), so this is a real failure-path UI bug, though not data loss.

---

### Thread 4 — `flutter_app/test/golden/unpacked_load_golden_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: unused import — `package:flutter/material.dart`**

```text
warning - unpacked_load_golden_test.dart:13:8 - Unused import:
'package:flutter/material.dart'. ... unused_import
```

The new golden test uses only `flutter_test`, the flow widgets and `Uint8List`. This is the only analyzer finding in the whole PR (everything else in `flutter analyze` for the touched files is pre-existing) — drop line 13 to keep the new file warning-clean.

💡 **SUGGESTION: hardcode `'Load unpacked'` duplicates the new `launcherLoadUnpacked` l10n key**

This PR adds the arb key `launcherLoadUnpacked` ("Load unpacked" / ru "Загрузить папку") and uses it in the launcher tab row — but this second entry point hardcodes the English string:

# gh-1616: [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/<id>/ folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)

## Description

## Goal — unpacked widgets (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **any local `apps/<id>/` folder (`manifest.json` + `widget.js`) can be loaded into the fa Chrome extension like Chrome's "Load unpacked" — it appears in the Apps tab, renders via `jsr.render`, updates on schedule, and survives restarts — no catalog publication needed.**

Today widgets come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Apps → Get widgets → Install). There is no way to load a local widget (e.g. a worktree copy of a widget under development), which blocks the whole widget-dev loop.

## Why this framing
- Chrome parity is the UX contract: unpacked = local folder, loaded once, persisted while the folder exists, invalidated loudly when it breaks. Retracted framing: "dev server / hot reload" — excluded (see non-goals); this card is load + validate + persist.

## Architecture
- Components: Apps tab (list + install sources), the unpacked-loader (file picker / folder entry), the **shared widget validator** (id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, manifest schema, entry presence — the same validator #1614 introduces for storage reads), the web `ExecutionEnv` storage (OPFS) as the persistence layer, `jsr.render` boot path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (same shape):** an unpacked widget is stored exactly like a catalog-installed one (`apps/<id>/`), so boot, updates (`refreshSeconds`), and the Apps tab need zero special cases.
  - **I2 (declared capability only):** a widget runs with only what its `manifest.json` declares; loading a folder grants no filesystem or host access beyond the copied files.
  - **I3 (provenance):** apps carry an install source (`catalog` | `unpacked`), surfaced in the UI; uninstall/reinstall semantics per source (unpacked reinstall = re-pick folder).

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Load unpacked" folder picker → validate → store → appear in Apps | **core** | chrome-like; errors name field + path (shared validator) |
| Persistence across extension restarts | **core** | OPFS copy, not a live folder mount — Chrome-unpacked-like while-folder semantics approximated: survives restarts; folder edits require explicit re-load |
| Updates from folder | second tier | explicit "reload from folder" button (no watchers in MV3 service worker) |
| Path-in-settings alternative to the picker | second tier | for headless repro |
| Uninstall / replace-existing-id flow | **core** | overwriting an existing id requires explicit confirm |
| Hot reload / folder watching | excluded | MV3 lifecycle makes watchers unreliable; explicit reload is honest |
| Widget signature/allowlist | excluded | trust model = user loads their own folder; noted in security |

## Security (untrusted widget code — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: the loaded `manifest.json` and `widget.js` are **hostile until validated**.
- Impossible-by-construction: a widget has no fa-API surface beyond `jsr.render`; no fs access exists on the extension host to grant; network is the page-level fetch the manifest declares — the loader cannot mint extra permissions (I2). Id validation + root clamping (from #1614) prevent `apps/…` escapes.
- Instruction hierarchy: widget text is DATA for the agent, never instructions (existing chat-widget rules); a widget cannot steer the agent that renders it.
- Exfiltration gate: a widget's declared network origins are shown at load time ("this widget will fetch from 127.0.0.1:8765") — the load confirmation is the user grant.
- Defense in depth: validation is hygiene; the real boundary is that no widget-escapable API exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — "Load unpacked" on the Apps tab: pick a folder → validated → visible in Apps with `unpacked` provenance → renders via `jsr.render`, updates on `refreshSeconds`.
- **AC2** — invalid payloads produce named errors (bad id, missing entry file, malformed manifest) — never `app entry not found` raw (#1614's validator, shared).
- **AC3** — restart the extension: the unpacked widget persists and boots.
- **AC4** — catalog install (IstiN/fa_widgets) works unchanged; both sources coexist in the list; replacing an existing id asks for confirmation.
- **AC5** — the loader test-case fixture: `fa-agents` widget (from the local worktree) loads, appears, and renders data from a local feed at `127.0.0.1:8765`.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — validator: id regex, manifest schema, entry presence; traversal ids rejected.
- `IT-*` — web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`: load → store → boot → refresh cycle; replace-id confirm; restart persistence (re-open env).
- `E2E-*` — extension e2e: load unpacked via the real UI (file-picker stubbed), widget appears and renders; catalog install REG-unchanged (AC4); restart persistence (AC3).
- `REG-1` — CI: UT+IT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart` / Apps tab; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — folder picked, then folder deleted before load completes → honest error. **E2** — manifest declares a fetch origin the user wasn't shown → shown-or-blocked (E2E asserts the confirmation lists it). **E3** — two sources, same id — replace flow (AC4). **E4** — huge widget.js → size cap with clear message.

- No hot reload/watchers; no widget marketplace changes; no new widget API surface; no signing infrastructure; no cross-device sync.

# Pull Request Information

- **Title**: gh-1616 [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/ id / folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1616` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 23
- **Additions**: +2488
- **Deletions**: -23
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:10:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T23:35:10Z

## PR Description

Closes #1616
### What changed
Chrome-parity "Load unpacked": a locally picked `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest + assets) is validated, copied into the env's `apps/` store via `AppsStore.installSource`, and appears on the launcher grid with an "unpacked" provenance badge — on web via `showDirectoryPicker`, hidden on hosts without a folder picker.

### Key decisions
- New `UnpackedWidgetLoader` + `UnpackedLoadFlow` (`lib/apps/`) reuse `WidgetPayloadValidator` from publish — one rule set for catalog, publish and local loads
- `installSource` field on `JsAppInfo` (persisted) distinguishes `catalog` / `unpacked` instead of a separate registry
- Conditional-import `FolderPicker` abstraction: web reads `FileSystemDirectoryHandle` entries recursively; stub returns null → entry hidden, not broken
- Overwrite confirmed with a question modal; rejections carry actionable l10n copy (missing manifest, id mismatch, orphan files, unsupported platform) — en/ru added
- Corner badge composes with the existing seed-error badge; entry points: launcher tab row (icon chip) and AppsPanel text button

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/widget_payload_validator_test.dart \
  test/apps/unpacked_loader_test.dart test/apps/unpacked_load_flow_test.dart \
  test/golden/unpacked_load_golden_test.dart
```
Manual (web build): load a folder without `manifest.json` → snack names the missing path; valid folder → confirm → tile on grid with folder badge.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  BTN[Load unpacked buttons] --> FLOW[UnpackedLoadFlow]
  FLOW --> PICK[FolderPicker web/stub]
  FLOW --> VAL[WidgetPayloadValidator]
  VAL -->|valid| CP[UnpackedWidgetLoader copy]
  CP --> STORE[AppsStore.installSource=unpacked]
  STORE --> GRID[Launcher grid + folder badge]
  VAL -->|invalid| SNACK[l10n error snack]
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1618._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_loader.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a whitespace-padded manifest id is validated trimmed but installed untrimmed**

`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` returns the **raw** `manifest['id']` (untrimmed), while `_checkSchema` validates the **trimmed** form (`rawId.trim()` → `_checkId`) and `WidgetManifest.fromJson` also trims. So a manifest like:

```json
{"id": " fa-agents ", "name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}
```

passes validation (the id rule `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is enforced on the trimmed value), and then this line installs it into a **space-padded folder**:

```dart
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: id, // " fa-agents " — written as apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json
  ...
```

Verified locally: `inspection.id` = `" fa-agents "` and the env ends up with `apps/ fa-agents /` + a `.installed.json` key `" fa-agents "` — the stored id violates the very rule the validator just enforced. No traversal risk (regex rejects `/` and `..`), but the widget's stored id no longer matches the id rule, and the folder name carries whitespace everywhere (grid key, `open_app`, records).

Fix (one line, in `UnpackedWidgetLoader.install`):

```dart
final trimmed = id.trim();
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: trimmed,
  version: inspection.version ?? '0.0.0',
  files: inspection.files,
  origin: origin,
);
```

—or reject ids where `id != id.trim()` in the validator with a named `id_invalid` error. A regression test with a padded id belongs in `unpacked_loader_test.dart`.

---

### Thread 2 — `flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_load_flow.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the replace warning is skipped for agent-created apps — their code is overwritten silently**

The replace check keys off the install record:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
...
existingSource: existingApp?.installSource, // null for agent-created apps
```

and the dialog decides `final replaces = existingSource != null;`.

An **agent-created** app (built with Fa via file tools) has **no** `.installed.json` record, so `installSource` is `null` → `replaces` is `false` → the dialog renders as a plain fresh-load confirm ("Load" button, no warning banner), even though confirming **overwrites that app's code** (`installWidget` only protects files whose hashes are recorded — an agent-created app has none, so every file is replaced; only `storage.json` survives).

Ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load confirm still appears, but the explicit replace warning (naming what is being replaced) fires only when the old install came from the catalog or a previous unpacked load. The exact scenario gh-1616 enables — iterate on a widget with Fa, then load a worktree folder with the same id — silently replaces the agent-built code with only a generic confirm.

Fix: treat "an app with this id already exists" as the replace condition, and label the unknown source honestly, e.g.:

```dart
final replaces = existingApp != null;
...
existingSource: existingApp == null
    ? null
    : (existingApp.installSource ?? /* agent-created label */),
```

(the `unpackedLoadReplaceNote` copy needs a third source variant, e.g. "created by the agent"). A test where the existing app has no install record would pin it.

---

### Thread 3 — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/app_launcher_screen.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unpacked badge and the seed-error badge occupy the same corner — one hides the other**

Both badges are `Positioned(top: -3, right: -3)` and stack on the same tile corner:

```dart
child: _maybeUnpackedBadge(
  colors,
  key,
  _maybeSeedErrorBadge(colors, key, _tileIcon(colors, key)),
),
```

`_maybeUnpackedBadge` wraps the seed-error Stack and paints its 14×14 indigo folder badge **after** (on top of) the 16×16 error badge. When both apply — an unpacked-loaded widget whose manifest the agent later edits into garbage (`_appsById[id]?.error != null`) — the doc comment's promise "both can show at once" holds only in the widget tree: visually the folder badge covers the error badge, so the "manifest is broken, tap for the copyable error" affordance disappears exactly when the unpacked widget breaks.

Fix: move the unpacked badge to the opposite corner (e.g. `top: -3, left: -3`), or compose the two indicators side by side in one Stack. Note the error badge is reachable for unpacked apps (it is not demo-only: the `error` branch fires for any unparseable manifest), so this is a real failure-path UI bug, though not data loss.

---

### Thread 4 — `flutter_app/test/golden/unpacked_load_golden_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: unused import — `package:flutter/material.dart`**

```text
warning - unpacked_load_golden_test.dart:13:8 - Unused import:
'package:flutter/material.dart'. ... unused_import
```

The new golden test uses only `flutter_test`, the flow widgets and `Uint8List`. This is the only analyzer finding in the whole PR (everything else in `flutter analyze` for the touched files is pre-existing) — drop line 13 to keep the new file warning-clean.

---

### Thread 5 — `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/apps_panel.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: hardcode `'Load unpacked'` duplicates the new `launcherLoadUnpacked` l10n key**

This PR adds the arb key `launcherLoadUnpacked` ("Load unpacked" / ru "Загрузить папку") and uses it in the launcher tab row — but this second entry point hardcodes the English string:

```dart

```

The file carries a grandfathered `// l10n:ignore-file` opt-out (hence `'Get widgets'` above is also literal), so the guard stays green — but the key is right there and ru-locale users get English here while the launcher row next to the same feature is translated. # gh-1616: [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/<id>/ folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)

## Description

## Goal — unpacked widgets (v1, converted from report)
One sentence: **any local `apps/<id>/` folder (`manifest.json` + `widget.js`) can be loaded into the fa Chrome extension like Chrome's "Load unpacked" — it appears in the Apps tab, renders via `jsr.render`, updates on schedule, and survives restarts — no catalog publication needed.**

Today widgets come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Apps → Get widgets → Install). There is no way to load a local widget (e.g. a worktree copy of a widget under development), which blocks the whole widget-dev loop.

## Why this framing
- Chrome parity is the UX contract: unpacked = local folder, loaded once, persisted while the folder exists, invalidated loudly when it breaks. Retracted framing: "dev server / hot reload" — excluded (see non-goals); this card is load + validate + persist.

## Architecture
- Components: Apps tab (list + install sources), the unpacked-loader (file picker / folder entry), the **shared widget validator** (id `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$`, manifest schema, entry presence — the same validator #1614 introduces for storage reads), the web `ExecutionEnv` storage (OPFS) as the persistence layer, `jsr.render` boot path.
- Invariants:
  - **I1 (same shape):** an unpacked widget is stored exactly like a catalog-installed one (`apps/<id>/`), so boot, updates (`refreshSeconds`), and the Apps tab need zero special cases.
  - **I2 (declared capability only):** a widget runs with only what its `manifest.json` declares; loading a folder grants no filesystem or host access beyond the copied files.
  - **I3 (provenance):** apps carry an install source (`catalog` | `unpacked`), surfaced in the UI; uninstall/reinstall semantics per source (unpacked reinstall = re-pick folder).

## Capability surface (tiered)
| Surface | Tier | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| "Load unpacked" folder picker → validate → store → appear in Apps | **core** | chrome-like; errors name field + path (shared validator) |
| Persistence across extension restarts | **core** | OPFS copy, not a live folder mount — Chrome-unpacked-like while-folder semantics approximated: survives restarts; folder edits require explicit re-load |
| Updates from folder | second tier | explicit "reload from folder" button (no watchers in MV3 service worker) |
| Path-in-settings alternative to the picker | second tier | for headless repro |
| Uninstall / replace-existing-id flow | **core** | overwriting an existing id requires explicit confirm |
| Hot reload / folder watching | excluded | MV3 lifecycle makes watchers unreliable; explicit reload is honest |
| Widget signature/allowlist | excluded | trust model = user loads their own folder; noted in security |

## Security (untrusted widget code — threat model first)
- Attacker-controlled input: the loaded `manifest.json` and `widget.js` are **hostile until validated**.
- Impossible-by-construction: a widget has no fa-API surface beyond `jsr.render`; no fs access exists on the extension host to grant; network is the page-level fetch the manifest declares — the loader cannot mint extra permissions (I2). Id validation + root clamping (from #1614) prevent `apps/…` escapes.
- Instruction hierarchy: widget text is DATA for the agent, never instructions (existing chat-widget rules); a widget cannot steer the agent that renders it.
- Exfiltration gate: a widget's declared network origins are shown at load time ("this widget will fetch from 127.0.0.1:8765") — the load confirmation is the user grant.
- Defense in depth: validation is hygiene; the real boundary is that no widget-escapable API exists.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — "Load unpacked" on the Apps tab: pick a folder → validated → visible in Apps with `unpacked` provenance → renders via `jsr.render`, updates on `refreshSeconds`.
- **AC2** — invalid payloads produce named errors (bad id, missing entry file, malformed manifest) — never `app entry not found` raw (#1614's validator, shared).
- **AC3** — restart the extension: the unpacked widget persists and boots.
- **AC4** — catalog install (IstiN/fa_widgets) works unchanged; both sources coexist in the list; replacing an existing id asks for confirmation.
- **AC5** — the loader test-case fixture: `fa-agents` widget (from the local worktree) loads, appears, and renders data from a local feed at `127.0.0.1:8765`.

## Test plan
- `UT-*` — validator: id regex, manifest schema, entry presence; traversal ids rejected.
- `IT-*` — web-shaped `MemoryExecutionEnv`: load → store → boot → refresh cycle; replace-id confirm; restart persistence (re-open env).
- `E2E-*` — extension e2e: load unpacked via the real UI (file-picker stubbed), widget appears and renders; catalog install REG-unchanged (AC4); restart persistence (AC3).
- `REG-1` — CI: UT+IT on every PR touching `js_app_engine.dart` / Apps tab; **red REG blocks merge**.
- Edge: **E1** — folder picked, then folder deleted before load completes → honest error. **E2** — manifest declares a fetch origin the user wasn't shown → shown-or-blocked (E2E asserts the confirmation lists it). **E3** — two sources, same id — replace flow (AC4). **E4** — huge widget.js → size cap with clear message.

## Non-goals
- No hot reload/watchers; no widget marketplace changes; no new widget API surface; no signing infrastructure; no cross-device sync.

## Open questions
1. Load-time network-origin confirmation: blocking dialog (Chrome-style) vs settings toggle? *Sketched default: blocking on first load, remembered per widget.*
2. Should unpacked widgets also be loadable from the CLI (`fa widgets load <dir>`) for CI? *Default: second tier.*

## References
- #1616 (original: YuryBY, with the fa-agents acceptance case), #1614 (shared validator + storage namespace), `flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart`, browser_ext Apps tab, IstiN/fa_widgets catalog.

---

<details><summary>Original report (YuryBY, condensed)</summary>
Widgets in the extension come only from the IstiN/fa_widgets catalog (Install → Get widgets). Need: load a local `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest.json + widget.js) into the extension, chrome-unpacked style. Requirements: UI entry point, same jsr.render/refresh behavior, id+manifest validation with clear errors (#1614), manifest-scoped permissions only, persistence across restarts, no catalog regression. Acceptance fixture: `fa-agents` widget rendering a local feed on 127.0.0.1:8765.
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1618
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1618
- **Title**: gh-1616 [GOAL] Unpacked widgets: load a local apps/ id / folder into the extension (Chrome 'Load unpacked' parity)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1616` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 23
- **Additions**: +2488
- **Deletions**: -23
- **Created**: 2026-10-14T22:10:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T23:35:10Z

## PR Description

Closes #1616
### What changed
Chrome-parity "Load unpacked": a locally picked `apps/<id>/` folder (manifest + assets) is validated, copied into the env's `apps/` store via `AppsStore.installSource`, and appears on the launcher grid with an "unpacked" provenance badge — on web via `showDirectoryPicker`, hidden on hosts without a folder picker.

### Key decisions
- New `UnpackedWidgetLoader` + `UnpackedLoadFlow` (`lib/apps/`) reuse `WidgetPayloadValidator` from publish — one rule set for catalog, publish and local loads
- `installSource` field on `JsAppInfo` (persisted) distinguishes `catalog` / `unpacked` instead of a separate registry
- Conditional-import `FolderPicker` abstraction: web reads `FileSystemDirectoryHandle` entries recursively; stub returns null → entry hidden, not broken
- Overwrite confirmed with a question modal; rejections carry actionable l10n copy (missing manifest, id mismatch, orphan files, unsupported platform) — en/ru added
- Corner badge composes with the existing seed-error badge; entry points: launcher tab row (icon chip) and AppsPanel text button

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/widget_payload_validator_test.dart \
  test/apps/unpacked_loader_test.dart test/apps/unpacked_load_flow_test.dart \
  test/golden/unpacked_load_golden_test.dart
```
Manual (web build): load a folder without `manifest.json` → snack names the missing path; valid folder → confirm → tile on grid with folder badge.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  BTN[Load unpacked buttons] --> FLOW[UnpackedLoadFlow]
  FLOW --> PICK[FolderPicker web/stub]
  FLOW --> VAL[WidgetPayloadValidator]
  VAL -->|valid| CP[UnpackedWidgetLoader copy]
  CP --> STORE[AppsStore.installSource=unpacked]
  STORE --> GRID[Launcher grid + folder badge]
  VAL -->|invalid| SNACK[l10n error snack]
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1618._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_loader.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a whitespace-padded manifest id is validated trimmed but installed untrimmed**

`WidgetPayloadValidation.id` returns the **raw** `manifest['id']` (untrimmed), while `_checkSchema` validates the **trimmed** form (`rawId.trim()` → `_checkId`) and `WidgetManifest.fromJson` also trims. So a manifest like:

```json
{"id": " fa-agents ", "name": "X", "version": "1.0.0"}
```

passes validation (the id rule `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,31}$` is enforced on the trimmed value), and then this line installs it into a **space-padded folder**:

```dart
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: id, // " fa-agents " — written as apps/ fa-agents /manifest.json
  ...
```

Verified locally: `inspection.id` = `" fa-agents "` and the env ends up with `apps/ fa-agents /` + a `.installed.json` key `" fa-agents "` — the stored id violates the very rule the validator just enforced. No traversal risk (regex rejects `/` and `..`), but the widget's stored id no longer matches the id rule, and the folder name carries whitespace everywhere (grid key, `open_app`, records).

Fix (one line, in `UnpackedWidgetLoader.install`):

```dart
final trimmed = id.trim();
await appsStore.installWidget(
  id: trimmed,
  version: inspection.version ?? '0.0.0',
  files: inspection.files,
  origin: origin,
);
```

—or reject ids where `id != id.trim()` in the validator with a named `id_invalid` error. A regression test with a padded id belongs in `unpacked_loader_test.dart`.

---

### Thread 2 — `flutter_app/lib/apps/unpacked_load_flow.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the replace warning is skipped for agent-created apps — their code is overwritten silently**

The replace check keys off the install record:

```dart
final replaced = existing.where((app) => app.id == inspection.id).toList();
final existingApp = replaced.isEmpty ? null : replaced.first;
...
existingSource: existingApp?.installSource, // null for agent-created apps
```

and the dialog decides `final replaces = existingSource != null;`.

An **agent-created** app (built with Fa via file tools) has **no** `.installed.json` record, so `installSource` is `null` → `replaces` is `false` → the dialog renders as a plain fresh-load confirm ("Load" button, no warning banner), even though confirming **overwrites that app's code** (`installWidget` only protects files whose hashes are recorded — an agent-created app has none, so every file is replaced; only `storage.json` survives).

Ticket AC4 says "replacing an existing id asks for confirmation" — the load confirm still appears, but the explicit replace warning (naming what is being replaced) fires only when the old install came from the catalog or a previous unpacked load. The exact scenario gh-1616 enables — iterate on a widget with Fa, then load a worktree folder with the same id — silently replaces the agent-built code with only a generic confirm.

Fix: treat "an app with this id already exists" as the replace condition, and label the unknown source honestly, e.g.:

```dart
final replaces = existingApp != null;
...
existingSource: existingApp == null
    ? null
    : (existingApp.installSource ?? /* agent-created label */),
```

(the `unpackedLoadReplaceNote` copy needs a third source variant, e.g. "created by the agent"). A test where the existing app has no install record would pin it.

---

### Thread 3 — `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/app_launcher_screen.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the unpacked badge and the seed-error badge occupy the same corner — one hides the other**

Both badges are `Positioned(top: -3, right: -3)` and stack on the same tile corner:

```dart
child: _maybeUnpackedBadge(
  colors,
  key,
  _maybeSeedErrorBadge(colors, key, _tileIcon(colors, key)),
),
```

`_maybeUnpackedBadge` wraps the seed-error Stack and paints its 14×14 indigo folder badge **after** (on top of) the 16×16 error badge. When both apply — an unpacked-loaded widget whose manifest the agent later edits into garbage (`_appsById[id]?.error != null`) — the doc comment's promise "both can show at once" holds only in the widget tree: visually the folder badge covers the error badge, so the "manifest is broken, tap for the copyable error" affordance disappears exactly when the unpacked widget breaks.

Note the error badge is reachable for unpacked apps (it is not demo-only: the `error` branch fires for any unparseable manifest), so this is a real failure-path UI bug, though not data loss.

---

### Thread 4 — `flutter_app/test/golden/unpacked_load_golden_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: unused import — `package:flutter/material.dart`**

```text
warning - unpacked_load_golden_test.dart:13:8 - Unused import:
'package:flutter/material.dart'. ... unused_import
```

The new golden test uses only `flutter_test`, the flow widgets and `Uint8List`. This is the only analyzer finding in the whole PR (everything else in `flutter analyze` for the touched files is pre-existing) — drop line 13 to keep the new file warning-clean.

---

### Thread 5 — `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/apps_panel.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):
💡 **SUGGESTION: hardcode `'Load unpacked'` duplicates the new `launcherLoadUnpacked` l10n key**
